newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields remain higher at noon.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields remain higher at noon.

text.p: Swedish bond yields remained higher at midday on Monday, still negatively affected by left-wing parties taking an unexpected lead in the first round of French elections on Sunday.
The crown was also hurt by the French news and softened to 4.5070 against the mark from 4.4910 late on Friday.

"Players fear either a delay (of Europe's economic and monetary union, EMU) or an easing of the (Maastricht) criteria as the Communists have opposed all kinds of cutbacks on spending," one dealer said.
Trade was quiet as Britain and the U.S. were closed.
"Yields remain at the opening levels and trade is very quiet," a trader said.
The six-month T-bill rose two basis points to 4.25 percent while the ten-year bond yield jumped six basis poiunts to 7.09 percent.
Players were waiting for the U.S. market to open on Tuesday.
They were also focusing on the second round of French elections on June 1, expecting to see more people voting for the ruling coalition.
